name: Ventriloquist Confirmation
definition: Present when a success message is emitted by the code path that requested a change rather than by the code path that verifiably committed it, so the confirmation can fire even if the change never happens.
symptom: User sees 'Saved', reloads, and the work is gone — the toast was the only thing that ever happened.
fix_pattern: Emit confirmation only from the store/persistence layer's success callback; the requester never announces on its own behalf.

other.citation: NN/g #1 Visibility of system status (Jakob Nielsen, nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/)
Shneiderman #3 Offer informative feedback
Apple HIG: feedback must reflect whether the command was actually carried out

illustration: Non-evidentiary illustration: a success toast fired from a click handler even though persistence was never invoked.

name: Forked Tally
definition: Present when a number announced to the user (toast, badge, summary) is computed at a different granularity or from a different unit than the number then displayed at the destination.
symptom: Told '2 added', arrives to find '(1)' — the system appears to have lost something it didn't.
fix_pattern: Both surfaces derive their count from one shared selector at one declared granularity; the announcement quotes the destination's own count.

other.citation: NN/g #1 Visibility of system status (Jakob Nielsen, nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/)
Shneiderman #4 Design dialogs to yield closure

illustration: Non-evidentiary illustration: success feedback counted leaf items while the destination summarized parent groups.

name: Celebrated No-Op
definition: Present when an action the system silently declines or dedupes (already present, at limit, invalid) still plays the full success feedback path.
symptom: Success toast and animation over an operation that changed nothing; the user believes a duplicate now exists.
fix_pattern: Branch feedback on the store's actual outcome enum (added / already-present / rejected), never on the fact that a handler ran.

other.citation: Apple HIG: show feedback when a command can't be carried out
NN/g #1 Visibility of system status (Jakob Nielsen, nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/)

illustration: Non-evidentiary illustration: adding an existing item produced success feedback even though deduplication made the operation a no-op.

name: Twin-Cap Trapdoor
definition: Present when a limit on a collection is enforced in two or more places with different values, such that an item can be accepted by one layer and discarded by another with no notice.
symptom: Adding an Nth item silently deletes it — accepted by the store, never rendered, gone on next look.
fix_pattern: One cap constant owned by the store, imported everywhere; reject at the single gate with visible feedback instead of truncating downstream.

other.citation: NN/g #5 Error prevention (Jakob Nielsen, nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/)
Shneiderman #6 Permit easy reversal of actions

illustration: Non-evidentiary illustration: storage accepted more pinned items than the view rendered, leaving the final accepted item invisible.

name: Parallax Count
definition: Present when a count and the collection it summarizes are read from different selectors or data paths, so they can disagree under any filter, type, or timing condition.
symptom: 'Insights (3)' floating above a list that says 'No insights yet'.
fix_pattern: The count is derived from the exact array the list renders — count = list.length by construction, not by parallel query.

other.citation: NN/g #1 Visibility of system status (Jakob Nielsen, nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/)
Shneiderman #3 Offer informative feedback

illustration: Non-evidentiary illustration: a count chip showed populated results while the adjacent list rendered an empty state from a different selector.

name: Coincidental Concord
definition: Present when two independently-derived readouts of the same state happen to agree in the tested configuration but are computed by paths that can diverge in other configurations.
symptom: Everything checks out in the demo collection, then the same screen lies in the collection that matters — and the earlier agreement bought it trust.
fix_pattern: Audit for shared derivation, not displayed agreement: any two surfaces showing one fact must trace to one selector, verified in source, across all type/collection variants.

other.citation: NN/g #1 Visibility of system status (Jakob Nielsen, nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/)

illustration: Non-evidentiary illustration: two mismatched selectors happened to agree in one state but diverged in the other tested states.

name: Day-One Deadbolt
definition: Present when a feature's only entry point renders behind a condition that is false in the fresh/default state, leaving the feature unreachable for a new user with no error emitted.
symptom: A shipped feature that no first-time user can find or trigger; nothing crashes, nothing explains.
fix_pattern: Test every entry point against the empty/fresh state; an entry point's render condition must be satisfiable before the feature has ever been used.

other.citation: Shneiderman #7 Support internal locus of control
NN/g #1 Visibility of system status (Jakob Nielsen, nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/)

illustration: Non-evidentiary illustration: the only entry point rendered behind a condition that was false for every new user.

name: Manifest Gap
definition: Present when a rendering or lookup switch has explicit branches for some item types but no branch (or a null-returning default) for others, so items of the unhandled type persist in state yet never appear.
symptom: Saved items exist but are invisible everywhere; the empty state can't even fire because the list is technically non-empty.
fix_pattern: Exhaustive type handling with a loud fallback: an unmatched type renders a visible error card or throws in development, never null.

other.citation: NN/g #9 Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors (Jakob Nielsen, nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/)
Apple HIG: show feedback when a command can't be carried out

illustration: Non-evidentiary illustration: a lookup omitted one supported type, returned null, and silently dropped those cards from every group.

name: Dropped Baton
definition: Present when closing or completing an overlay leaves document.activeElement on body (or a stale node) instead of returning focus to a live, correct successor element.
symptom: Keyboard and screen-reader users are dumped to the top of the page after every dialog; sighted mouse users never notice.
fix_pattern: Capture the restore target by stable identity before the overlay opens, and re-resolve it against the live DOM at close time — never trust a remembered node across re-render.

other.citation: NN/g #3 User control and freedom (Jakob Nielsen, nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/)

illustration: Non-evidentiary illustration: closing a dialog removed its opener before the restore target was captured, leaving focus on the document body.

name: Ouroboros Trigger
definition: Present when a decision (reorder, threshold, snap, layout choice) reads a value that the decision's own effect or animation mutates, allowing one input to produce repeated re-triggering instead of one settled outcome.
symptom: One drag produces flickering oscillation, rubber-banding, or dozens of state commits before (or without) settling.
fix_pattern: Decide from a stable model snapshot (logical positions), never from rendered geometry the effect animates; commit once per gesture.

other.citation: Shneiderman #4 Design dialogs to yield closure
NN/g #1 Visibility of system status (Jakob Nielsen, nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/)

illustration: Non-evidentiary illustration: drag reordering measured geometry that its own animation changed, causing repeated commits and oscillation.

name: Undead Understudy
definition: Present when a placeholder or interim mechanism (fake animation, optimistic stub, temporary signal) still runs after the real mechanism it stood in for has shipped, producing multiple signals for one state change.
symptom: Two or three animations announce one event; the redundancy reads as glitching, not polish.
fix_pattern: Every stand-in ships with a removal condition tied to its replacement's landing; retiring the stub is part of the real feature's definition of done.

other.citation: NN/g #1 Visibility of system status (Jakob Nielsen, nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/)
Shneiderman #3 Offer informative feedback

illustration: Non-evidentiary illustration: a legacy nudge animation remained after real reflow was added, so multiple cues competed for one state change.

name: Amnesiac Relaunch
definition: Present when in-progress user work or configuration survives neither reload nor relaunch, and no warning precedes the loss.
symptom: Accidental refresh, crash, or tab close erases everything since the last explicit save — silently.
fix_pattern: Persist session state continuously (draft autosave, restoration on launch); if restoration is genuinely impossible, warn before unload.

other.citation: Apple HIG: restore state on launch
NN/g #5 Error prevention (Jakob Nielsen, nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/)

illustration: Non-evidentiary illustration: an in-progress configuration disappeared on reload without a warning or recovery route.

name: Evaporated Undo
definition: Present when the only affordance that could reverse an action unmounts, disables, or disappears as a consequence of that same action.
symptom: The mistake removes the very control that would fix the mistake; recovery requires support or re-creation from scratch.
fix_pattern: Undo lives above the mutated scope (global toast with undo, command stack), never inside the component the action destroys.

other.citation: Shneiderman #6 Permit easy reversal of actions
NN/g #3 User control and freedom (Jakob Nielsen, nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/)
Apple HIG: undoability, not destructiveness, gates confirmation

illustration: Non-evidentiary illustration: a removed item could not be restored because its undo control unmounted with the item.

name: Silent Curfew
definition: Present when a session, hold, or edit window expires on a timer the user was not warned about and cannot extend, and expiry discards entered data or context.
symptom: User returns from a brief interruption to find the form cleared or the session dead, work gone.
fix_pattern: Warn before expiry, offer extension, and preserve entered data across re-authentication so nothing must be retyped.
